entity_title: Residency visa then residence permit at AIMA
fact_text: A third-country professional moving to Portugal follows a two-step model: the consulate issues a residency visa valid for only 4 months and 2 entries, within which the holder must apply for a residence permit at AIMA (the immigration agency). The visa is an entry document, not the residence title itself.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the long-stay visa is the residence permit. Actually the residency visa is valid just 4 months/2 entries and only lets you enter to lodge the residence-permit application at AIMA. Action: schedule the AIMA residence-permit step immediately on arrival, before the 4-month visa lapses.

entity_title: Residence visa may be issued without an AIMA appointment
fact_text: If no AIMA appointment is available when the consulate issues the residence visa, the visa is affixed without an appointment link and the holder must instead request the residence-permit appointment through a designated AIMA online form after arriving in Portugal (for highly skilled workers, choosing subject 'Residence Permit with Consular Visa (Highly Skilled)').

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the residence visa comes with a booked AIMA appointment. Actually the visa is often issued with no appointment attached. Action: on arrival, submit the AIMA contact form selecting 'Residence Permit' > 'Residence Permit with Consular Visa (Highly Skilled/Non-CPLP)' using your own personal email.

entity_title: EU Blue Card (Cartão Azul UE) salary threshold
fact_text: For highly qualified staff, Portugal's EU Blue Card (Cartão Azul UE, art. 121-A) is an alternative to the ordinary work-residence route. It requires a work contract or promise of at least 6 months paying an annual salary of at least 1.5 times the national average gross annual salary (1.2 times in the cases of art. 61-A(2)), plus health cover and proof of qualifications.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed all foreign hires use the same work visa. Actually a highly qualified third-country hire can instead take the EU Blue Card, which imposes a specific salary floor (1.5x, or 1.2x national average gross salary). Action: check whether the offered salary clears the Blue Card threshold, which unlocks EU-wide mobility a national permit does not.

entity_title: Blue Card holder can move to Portugal after 18 months
fact_text: A third-country national who has held an EU Blue Card in another EU Member State for at least 18 months can move to Portugal to carry out a highly qualified activity and bring family members, obtaining a Portuguese residence authorisation without the full consular residence-visa route.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed every third-country hire must start over with a consular visa. Actually an existing EU Blue Card held 18+ months in another Member State lets the worker relocate to Portugal under intra-EU mobility. Action: if the employee already holds a Blue Card elsewhere, use the mobility route instead of a new consular application.

entity_title: Apostilled criminal-record certificate for residence visa
fact_text: A residency visa application requires a criminal-record certificate issued by the authority of the applicant's nationality (or of a country where they lived over a year), bearing the Hague Apostille or otherwise legalised. This must be obtained in the home country before applying at the consulate.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed home-country documents are accepted as-is. Actually the criminal-record certificate must carry a Hague Apostille or consular legalisation. Action: order and apostille the police certificate at home before departure, since obtaining it after arriving in Portugal is far harder.

entity_title: Family reunification is filed at AIMA before the consulate
fact_text: To bring family members, the resident third-country national must first request the family-reunification concession at AIMA in Portugal; only after a favourable AIMA decision can the family members lodge their residency visa applications at a consular post abroad.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the family applies for visas at the consulate first. Actually the sponsor must obtain the reunification concession from AIMA in Portugal before any family visa is filed. Action: start the AIMA reunification request once you hold a residence permit, before family members approach the consulate.

entity_title: Fiscal representative needed once a tax relationship forms
fact_text: A NIF (tax number) can be obtained as a non-resident without naming a fiscal representative. But once a third-country non-resident forms a tax relationship in Portugal (e.g. signs an employment or rental contract), they must within 15 days appoint a Portugal-resident fiscal representative or subscribe to an electronic notification channel. This is optional for EU/EEA residents but obligatory for third-country residents.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a fiscal representative is always required just to get a NIF, or never required. Actually it is not needed to obtain the NIF, but becomes mandatory within 15 days of forming a tax relationship while still non-resident in a third country (unlike EU/EEA residents, for whom it is optional). Action: appoint a fiscal representative or subscribe to electronic notifications when signing your first PT contract.

entity_title: IFICI regime replaces NHR, with strict conditions
fact_text: The former Non-Habitual Resident (NHR/RNH) regime is closed to new entrants; the successor is IFICI (tax incentive for scientific research and innovation, art. 58-A EBF), giving a special 20% IRS rate on Portuguese category A/B income. It requires not having been tax-resident in Portugal in the previous 5 years, becoming tax resident now, working in a narrow list of qualified activities, and never having benefited from NHR.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed newcomers still get the old NHR 20% deal automatically. Actually NHR is closed and its successor IFICI is far narrower - only certain qualified professions, requires 5 years prior non-residence, and bars anyone who ever used NHR. Action: confirm the role sits in an IFICI-eligible activity before promising the 20% rate.

fact_text: Under art. 16 CIRS you become a Portuguese tax resident if you spend more than 183 days (consecutive or not) in any 12-month period starting or ending in the year. Crucially, you can also be treated as resident with fewer days if you hold a home in Portugal in conditions suggesting you intend to keep it as your habitual residence, and a 'day of presence' counts any full or partial day that includes an overnight stay.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you only become tax-resident after 183 days. Actually renting/holding a habitual home can make you resident with fewer days, and partial days with an overnight count as full days. Action: plan the move date and IFICI/split-year position around when residency actually triggers, not just a 183-day count.

fact_text: To get a NISS (social security number), a third-country national must present all of: passport, work visa, and residence permit (temporary or permanent) plus proof of the work situation. The employer can request the NISS as the worker's legal representative and must register the employment in Segurança Social Direta.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a NISS needs only ID. Actually third-country nationals must show passport + work visa + residence permit, unlike EU/EEA/Swiss citizens who can use a single ID document. Action: have the residence permit issued before the NISS request, or have the employer file it as legal representative once the work contract exists.

entity_title: SNS user number alone does not guarantee coverage
fact_text: Any foreigner with legal residence can get an SNS 'numero de utente', assigned on the first visit to a public health unit. But holding the number alone does not guarantee that the SNS covers your care costs - your record must also link your ID, Portuguese NIF, full Portuguese address and a valid residence permit.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed getting the SNS user number equals free public healthcare. Actually the number alone does not guarantee cost coverage; the record must also carry your NIF, address and valid residence permit. Action: register the residence permit, NIF and address at your health centre, do not stop at obtaining the number.

entity_title: Foreign licence exchange deadline and country rules
fact_text: A non-resident may drive on a foreign licence for 185 days; once resident in Portugal you must exchange it for a Portuguese licence within 2 years (for countries with a bilateral/reciprocity agreement or that adhere to the road-traffic conventions). Licences from non-convention countries are not valid to drive on and must be exchanged immediately, requiring a Portuguese driving exam per category.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed any foreign licence can be driven on indefinitely or simply swapped. Actually residents get 2 years to exchange (agreement/convention countries), while non-convention-country licences are invalid at once and require a full PT driving exam per category. Action: check whether your country has an exchange agreement with Portugal; if not, budget for a driving test.
